observations: body L1: the dash of «al–Battānī» is a long dash (5.5 pt); the name is not letter-spaced here. A speck stands under the comma after «reperire».

body L3-L4: both rules give the right ascension counted from the beginning of Capricorn, that is, increased by 90°. When the star rises, the point of the equator rising with it has the right ascension α − P + 90° (α the right ascension of the star from the first point of Aries, P its semidiurnal arc), so the oblique ascension of the degree rising with the star, increased by P, is α + 90°. When the star sets, the point of the equator then rising has the right ascension α + P + 90°, so the second rule holds with the oblique ascension of the degree rising at that moment, the nadir of the degree setting with the star (the ascension of the nadir, as on p. 196), diminished by P; the oblique ascension of the setting degree itself differs from it by 180° and twice the ascensional difference of that degree.
body L4: the minus sign is printed as a long dash (9.8 pt); it is set as a minus sign.

body L7-L15: the figure stands at the left of lines 7 to 15, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridian as a circle; the horizon, the equator EE′ and the axis from the centre O to the pole P as straight lines; the ecliptic, from the left of the circle through the first point of Aries, K and I to R, and the circle of declination of the star, from P through S and I to A on the equator, as arcs; the bold italic letters and the sign of Aries. The pole P is not named in the text.
body L7: a speck stands over the s of «Est».
body L7-L14: the letters of the figure named in these lines are upright, in the type of the text; in L15 and L16 they are italic.

body L14-L16: the relations are right: O, where the horizon cuts the equator, is 90° from the meridian, so EO is a quadrant, OA = EA − 90° and ♈A = ♈O + EA − 90°; the figure shows the rising of a star of northern declination, whose circle of declination meets the equator at A below the horizon.
body L15-L16: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.4 and 9.8 pt); they are set as minus signs.
body L16: a speck stands over the E of the first «EA».
body L19: the head of the notes on chapter 25, «Ad» and «caput» in small capitals, in the larger type of the heads.
body L20: in the head, the dash after «a)» measures 10.1 pt and the dash of «36–37» 5.1 pt; transcribed as a dash and a long dash.
body L21: the hyphen of «tem-» is printed short (1.6 pt), like a point.
body L25: «regulae haec sunt» is printed so.
body L27-L29: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.5 to 10.2 pt); they are set as minus signs.

body L27-L33: the rules render al-Battānī's text of chapter 25 (p. 36) step by step: the cosine of the obliquity taken from 2R (120 parts) gives the sinus longissimus, the cosine of δ′ taken from 2R the sinus crescens, R sin ε/cos δ′ the sine of the obliquitas aequata, and the product of the four factors the sine of the variatio; the solstitial distance of the culminating degree is counted in right ascension, as the text says.
body L31: the bar of the last fraction is printed broken near its right end, with a dot in the break; it is drawn whole. The fractions are set wider than in the print.
